vectors.description: Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): the CTV-01 envelope in RFC 8785 (JCS) form: UTF-8, no duplicate member names, no surrogate or noncharacter. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message.

Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): a string value written as the ESCAPED valid surrogate pair "\ud83d\ude00" (the bytes contain the twelve ASCII characters of the two escapes): a valid pair is allowed. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message.

Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): the same character U+1F600 written LITERALLY in UTF-8 (bytes f0 9f 98 80): allowed; CTV-12 and CTV-13 denote the same character with different bytes. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message.

Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): member names that differ only in case ("a", "A") and the same name "a" at two different levels are not duplicates. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message.

Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): the integer 1152921504606846976 (2^60) in payload.args: steps 2-4 add no limit on the magnitude or precision of JSON numbers (Core §5.2); later steps and field constraints still apply. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message.

Core §5.2 pipeline steps 2-4 (raw bytes): payload.args.count is an integer of 5000 digits, beyond the 4300-digit integer conversion limit some JSON libraries apply by default: steps 2-4 add no limit on the magnitude or precision of JSON numbers, so it is accepted here as a number. Accepted: well-formed I-JSON text only — not a valid, authenticated or authorized message, and no claim that it can be canonicalized (RFC 8785) or that its field accepts it.

State §3.1.2: Valid SET structure — runtime MUST reject when serialized value exceeds 1,048,576 bytes with error code 'payload_too_large'. Size enforcement is programmatic, not schema-level. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.2 rule 6.

State §3.1.2: Valid state_set audit record — the audit event MUST NOT include the entry value. The audit record stores payload_hash (SHA-256), not raw payload content. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.2.
State §3.1.3: Valid DELETE — after logical deletion, the entry MUST remain visible via SNAPSHOT within its retention period. DELETE does not accelerate physical removal. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.3.
State §3.1.3: Valid state_delete audit record — when audit_required is true, DELETE MUST generate an audit event of type 'state_delete'. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.3.
State §3.1.4: Valid QUERY — runtime MUST NOT return entries that the requesting agent is not authorised to access, regardless of filter criteria. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.4.
State §3.1.4: Valid QUERY for another agent's entries without a grant — result MUST be empty (not an error). Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.4.
State §3.1.4: Valid QUERY with time-based filter — results MUST be ordered by created_at ascending (oldest first) for deterministic pagination. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.4.
State §3.1.4: Valid QUERY with limit 1500 — runtime MUST clamp to maximum 1000 entries per query, not reject the request. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.4.
State §3.1.4: Valid QUERY with limit 2000 — MUST succeed (clamped to 1000), not rejected. Requests with limit exceeding 1000 MUST be clamped. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.1.4.

State §3.2.1: Valid SNAPSHOT with future as_of and filter — runtime MUST return error code 'invalid_request' for future timestamps. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.1.
State §3.2.1: Valid SNAPSHOT with very old as_of — runtime MUST reject when as_of predates the oldest retained version with error 'invalid_request'. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.1.

State §3.2.1: Valid SNAPSHOT with historical as_of predating available history — runtime MUST return error 'invalid_request' with details { snapshot_unavailable: true, oldest_available: ... }. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.1.

State §3.2.2: Valid PURGE operation — after PURGE, SNAPSHOT queries for the key at any time MUST return null for the entry value. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.2.

State §3.2.2: Valid state_revoke audit record from PURGE — grant revocation audit events MUST be generated for each revoked grant during PURGE. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.2 step 6.

State §3.2.2: Valid state_purge audit record — the audit event MUST NOT contain the purged value (erasure must not be defeated by the audit trail). Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.2. The purged entry has no retention period: within_retention false, entry_retained_until null (State §3.2.2).

State §3.2.2: Valid PURGE operation structure — runtime MUST deny PURGE to agents with only arsiaprotocol.state.* wildcard capability. arsiaprotocol.state.purge MUST be explicitly granted. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.2.

State §3.2.2: Valid PURGE operation — repeated PURGE without a later write is idempotent: it MUST return success with the original purged_at and MUST NOT generate a second audit event (Idempotency rule 2). Per ARSIA-State.md §3.2.2.

State §3.3.1: Valid state_grant audit record — when audit_required is true, GRANT MUST generate an audit event of type 'state_grant'. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.3.1.
State §3.3.2: Valid REVOKE — after revocation, the grantee MUST be denied access on the next operation. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.3.2.

State §3.3.2: Valid state_revoke audit record — when audit_required is true, REVOKE MUST generate an audit event of type 'state_revoke'. Per ARSIA-State.md §3.3.2.
